tables.title: Variance Explained
notes: Based on the correlation matrix (standardized variables).

tables.title: Component Loadings
notes: Loadings are correlations between each variable and the component.

assumptions.message: KMO = 0.65 (mediocre). The correlations are compact enough for this analysis.
The variables are correlated enough to be reduced.

interpretation.text: A principal component analysis of 4 variables (N = 50) retained 2 components, explaining 86.8% of the total variance. The first component explained 62.0%.

title: Principal Component Analysis
code:
library(ggnext)
# Principal component analysis: murder, assault, urban_pop, rape
vars <- c("murder", "assault", "urban_pop", "rape")
d <- data[complete.cases(data[, vars]), , drop = FALSE]
x <- d[vars]
pca <- prcomp(x, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
eigenvalues <- pca$sdev^2
variance <- data.frame(component = seq_along(eigenvalues), eigenvalue = eigenvalues,
                       proportion = eigenvalues / sum(eigenvalues), cumulative = cumsum(eigenvalues) / sum(eigenvalues))
n_comp <- 2
# Loadings: correlations between the variables and the component scores
loadings <- cor(x, pca$x[, seq_len(n_comp), drop = FALSE])
communality <- rowSums(loadings^2)
# Sampling adequacy (KMO) and Bartlett's test of sphericity
R <- cor(x)
Q <- solve(R)
A <- -Q / sqrt(outer(diag(Q), diag(Q)))   # anti-image (partial) correlations
off <- row(R) != col(R)
kmo <- sum(R[off]^2) / (sum(R[off]^2) + sum(A[off]^2))
bartlett_chi <- -(nrow(x) - 1 - (2 * ncol(x) + 5) / 6) * log(det(R))
bartlett_df <- ncol(x) * (ncol(x) - 1) / 2
bartlett_p <- pchisq(bartlett_chi, bartlett_df, lower.tail = FALSE)
p_scree <- ggnext(variance, aes(component, eigenvalue)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, dash = "4 4") +
  labs(title = "Scree plot", x = "Component", y = "Eigenvalue") +
  theme_modern()
scores <- data.frame(PC1 = pca$x[, 1], PC2 = pca$x[, 2])
p_scores <- ggnext(scores, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Component scores") +
  theme_modern()
p_scores <- p_scores + labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", 100 * variance$proportion[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", 100 * variance$proportion[2]))
